item.title: Wrist Arthroplasty & Biomechanics — 2026-08-02
item.itunes:author: Eric R. Wagner, MD, MSc
item.description: Weekly Wrist Arthroplasty & Biomechanics Literature Digest — 2026-08-02 Pulled from PubMed (NCBI E-utilities) across the six target journals — JBJS Am, J Hand Surg Am, Plast Reconstr Surg, J Wrist Surg, J Hand Surg Eur Vol, and Hand Clinics. This track covers (a) total wrist arthroplasty / wrist implant replacement, (b) wrist biomechanics (native-carpal kinematics, ligament/TFCC/DRUJ mechanics, cadaveric/finite-element/in-vitro/4D-CT work), and — newly added to the scope this run — (c) intercarpal ligament injuries (scapholunate, lunotriquetral, midcarpal instability, perilunate: diagnosis, open/reconstructive treatment, biomechanics) and (d) wrist arthritis treatments (SLAC/SNAC and radiocarpal/midcarpal OA; proximal row carpectomy, limited and total fusion, denervation, salvage). Arthroscopy-technique papers (covered by the wrist-arthroscopy track), pure distal-radius-fracture-fixation papers with no biomechanical or carpal-ligament/arthritis focus, basic-science/molecular work, and letters/errata/replies/editorials were excluded. Author line = first & senior author; corresponding-author institution listed per article. Window used: the last 90 days by publication date (2026-05-04 → 2026-08-02). The 7-, 14-, and 30-day windows each returned fewer than eight qualifying articles once papers already covered in the 2026-07-31 digest were removed, so the window was widened per this track's protocol. All 22 articles below are new to this track — every PMID was checked against the 2026-07-31 digest and duplicates were dropped. Scope note: the two newly added areas (c) and (d) were checked for a one-time 18-month backfill. The existing 2026-07-31 digest already covers scapholunate and midcarpal material, so the self-detecting backfill condition was not met and the full 18-month sweep was skipped; the broadened 90-day window below seeds the new areas instead. (For the record, an 18-month Query B sweep returns 153 records — far more than one weekly digest can carry.) According to PubMed, 22 articles qualified. JBJS Am, Plastic & Reconstructive Surgery, and Hand Clinics had no qualifying articles in this window (the Hand Clinics wrist hit was a transradial-amputation review, out of scope; the JBJS and PRS wrist hits were carpal-tunnel and soft-tissue papers). --- J Wrist Surg (11) The dominant journal this window — SLAC/SNAC salvage arthrodesis, perilunate reconstruction, and carpal-alignment imaging. Long-Term Functional Outcomes After Volar Capsulodesis for Treatment of Scapholunate Ligament Injuries: An 18-Year Experience Aida K Sarcon & Steven L Moran — Mayo Clinic, Rochester, MN, USA Single-institution observational series (2004–2022; 28 patients, mean follow-up 86 months) of volar scapholunate capsulodesis using a strip of the long radiolunate ligament for injuries with a torn volar SL component; mean DASH was 16.4 and PRWE 24.6, grip reached 79% of the contralateral side, 79% returned to prior work, and only two patients required secondary surgery.

item.title: Wrist Arthroplasty & Biomechanics — 2026-07-31
item.itunes:author: Eric R. Wagner, MD, MSc
item.description: Weekly Wrist Arthroplasty & Biomechanics Literature Digest — 2026-07-31 Pulled from PubMed (NCBI E-utilities) across the six target journals — JBJS Am, J Hand Surg Am, Plast Reconstr Surg, J Wrist Surg, J Hand Surg Eur Vol, and Hand Clinics. Restricted to articles focused on (a) total wrist arthroplasty / wrist implant replacement (implant design, survivorship, revision, outcomes; includes DRUJ/ulnar-head prosthetic arthroplasty and wrist hemiarthroplasty) or (b) wrist biomechanics — native-wrist and carpal kinematics/kinetics, ligament/TFCC/DRUJ mechanics and load transfer, and implant-related cadaveric, finite-element, in-vitro, and dynamic-imaging studies. Arthroscopy-technique papers (covered by the wrist-arthroscopy track), pure clinical fracture-fixation outcome papers with no biomechanical focus, letters/errata/replies/editorials, and non-wrist items were excluded. Author line = first & senior author; corresponding-author institution listed per article. According to PubMed, 22 articles qualified. This first run widened the window to the last ~18 months by publication date (2025-01-01 → 2026-07-31) to build a fuller sample in a niche literature; going forward this track runs weekly over the prior 7 days and widens the window when the week is thin. JBJS Am and Plastic & Reconstructive Surgery had no qualifying wrist-arthroplasty or wrist-biomechanics articles in this window (the JBJS wrist hits were basic-science carpal-tunnel work, out of scope). --- J Hand Surg Am (7) The busiest journal this window — cadaveric and finite-element biomechanics plus an implant-accuracy study. In Vitro Kinetic and Kinematic Analysis of a Recently Designed Total Wrist Implant Salvatore M Cavallaro & Frederick W Werner — SUNY Upstate Medical University, Syracuse, NY, USA Cadaveric in-vitro study (6 fresh-frozen wrists on a motion simulator) comparing range of motion and tendon forces before and after implanting a recently designed total wrist arthroplasty; the flexion–extension arc fell to ~51°, extension and radioulnar deviation were significantly reduced, and carpal–radial component impingement occurred in 4 of 6 wrists in radial deviation. PubMed · DOI Accuracy of Implant Placement Using Augmented Reality-assisted Technique in Total Wrist Arthroplasty Shimpei Watanabe & Takuji Iwamoto — Keio University School of Medicine, Tokyo, Japan Cadaveric study (14 limbs from 7 cadavers) in which an AR-assisted, three-point-registration TWA performed by a TWA-naïve surgeon was compared side-to-side with surgeon-guided TWA; AR improved the accuracy and consistency of radial- and carpal-component placement.
